questions.q: Before a currency can be used anywhere in Oracle Fusion, what must happen to it?
options: It must be explicitly enabled, typically through the Manage Currencies task
It must be assigned a conversion rate type of Fixed only
It must be converted to USD first
Nothing, all ISO currencies are automatically usable
questions.explain: Currencies ship predefined in Oracle Fusion but must be explicitly enabled before they can be used on a ledger or transaction.

questions.q: Which of the four predefined conversion rate types requires the preparer to manually enter a rate, with no automatic value supplied?
options: Corporate
User
Fixed
Spot
questions.explain: The User rate type is the one exception to automated rates — a rate must be typed in manually during journal entry.

questions.q: What is the main characteristic of a Corporate conversion rate?
options: It requires manual entry every time, like the User rate type
It changes multiple times per day to reflect market swings
It is a standard, deliberately smoothed rate set by senior finance management and used over a period of time
It can only be used for USD transactions
questions.explain: Corporate rates are set by management and intentionally smoothed so reported results don't fluctuate with every daily market move.

questions.q: When is a Fixed conversion rate type most appropriate?
options: Only for a ledger's functional currency
It cannot actually be used in Oracle Fusion
For highly volatile currencies that change daily
For currencies that are pegged to another currency by policy and don't need daily recalculation
questions.explain: Fixed rates suit currencies pegged to another currency, since the rate doesn't need to be recalculated daily.

questions.q: What is the difference between a ledger's functional currency and a transaction's currency?
options: They must always be identical
The functional currency is the one fixed currency a ledger's balances are stated in, while the transaction currency is whatever currency a specific transaction was originally entered in
Functional currency only applies to secondary ledgers
Transaction currency is set once per fiscal year
questions.explain: The functional currency is fixed as one of the ledger's 4 C's, while individual transactions may be entered in a different transaction currency requiring conversion.
